item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for your feedback!

Eh, in my opinion, this feels more like a inspiration of SCP-513 just that the effects of the bell are more violent.

Bugger, I didn't know that one. I wonder now if this has enough to stand on it's own. I am tying it in to historical people and events, and it has different effects, so possibly.

show spoilers
hide spoilers

Honestly, the name came first (after reading Pink Floyd's wikipedia article!). Then thoughts started circulating: a bell that divides people somehow. Option 1: It actually splits them in two somehow, nah, don't like it. Option 2: The sound has an effect on their aggression (stimulates the amygdala? enhanced fight-or-flight reaction?) and causes them to attack other people. From there, I started reading up on the history of bells and how to tie it in to the SCP.
Simultaneously, while I love cool monster SCPs, I also like SCPs where there's a smidge of plausibility. I recently re-read 096 and his rage issues. What if a similar violent rage happened, but to normal people, not a superhuman impossible beastie. We'd be exhausted after a short time and likely to injure ourselves as well as others. Afterwards there would be profound psychological impacts - suicide likely.

How DID they renovate it exactly? You can't leave that blank. While the foundation does leave some stuff away, you have to give a little bit of context.

Well, this is just an ideas critique/greenlight, not a finished draft. But I imagine it's removal of tarnish, re-attachment of the clapper, suspension from a frame, addition of a rope. I might add something if I draft an article, but it's not really important.

I'd recommend you keeping it secret since some SCPs have their locations of where they were found redacted or with a black box. THAT'S what the Foundation does to keep things secret.

Eh, I'm torn on this. The SCP has been removed from the discovery location (and there's nothing anomalous about the location istself). In universe, the SCP data is only available to SCP personnel anyway. I'm not sure what benefit there would be to redacting it, there's not really a reason to keep the location secret. I don't want to redact just for the sake of it.

item.title: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/History

Elevator Pitch: An archaic bell that when rung instils extreme feelings of revulsion and loathing towards other humans (to the point of violence)

Central Narrative:
Discovery log - This will describe the findings of the archaeological dig where the bell was found. Summarised:
Discovered in the Fens near Crowland Abbey, England.
Surrounded by human skeletal remains bearing signs of violence (broken bones, crushed skulls, incision marks, burn marks, etc.
Dated to circa 710 CE.
Unusual bronze composition (higher than normal tin percentage; presence of antimony - unknown at time bell casting)
Inscription on bell 'belli munus' (Latin for 'gift of war')
Essentially, the discovery log will hint at something unusual, setting the stage for the incident log, where the anomalous properties were discovered.

Incident log - This will describe what happened when a historical society/museum renovated it and rang it for the first time: all attendees consumed with revulsion and/or loathing, leading to much violence including deaths and serious injuries. Probably a description from security and/or news camera footage at the venue.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Addendum 1 - this will link the bell to Guthlac of Crowland - an ascetic hermit monk who later had an abbey built for him by the king of Mercia, and was said to be plagued by demons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guthlac_of_Crowland). The implication will be that the demons made him create the bell during his isolation.
Addendum 2 - this will briefly describe some lost notes from the Hemony brothers (real world bell founders from the 1600s), with a design identical to the Fens bell - plus documentation that several of these were manufactured and sold (to unknown parties). And possibly notes for an 'improved' design.

Additional Notes:
I'd like to have a sound clip of the bell to either play automatically a certain amount of time after opening the article (creepy but not really within the SCP format) or after clicking one/many links with appropriate warnings/security credentials ('Confirm level 3 access', 'Confirm you are alone', 'Confirm you are shackled' etc.).
